turns.user: Tìm 2 tin AI hôm nay trên web, viết bản tin ngắn có link nguồn. Chỉ dùng 2 nguồn vừa tìm được.
turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là hai tin tức về trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) hôm nay:

1. **Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous**  
   Bài viết này thảo luận về việc AI cung cấp hướng dẫn sức khỏe với quy mô chưa từng có, nhưng cũng chỉ ra rằng những câu trả lời chính xác từ AI có thể gây ra những rủi ro. Chính phủ đang thúc đẩy việc sử dụng AI trong chăm sóc sức khỏe, nhưng cần phải xem xét các vấn đề đạo đức liên quan đến việc này.  
   [Đọc thêm tại STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/ai-health-advice-accuracy-messaging-risk-behavioral-benchmarking)

2. **Banks push online banking, then blame us when we get hacked**  
   Bài viết này nêu lên những lo ngại về việc AI có thể ảnh hưởng đến cuộc sống hàng ngày của con người, từ việc quản lý tài chính đến việc mất kiểm soát trước công nghệ. Tác giả chỉ ra rằng sự phát triển của AI có thể dẫn đến những vấn đề nghiêm trọng hơn trong tương lai.  
   [Đọc thêm tại USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/columnist/2026/11/10/ai-online-banking-vulnerable-hacking/92588938007)

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. items.summary:
One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] # Someone drained my bank account. Then the real nightmare began | Opinion

## Over time, AI is going to turn our brains to mush. People won't be able to remember phone numbers, basic grammar or directions to places they've visited once or twice without consulting AI overlords.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.
